column1: # comment: "Universal determinacy alignments. FORMAL GROUNDING: gmeow:Determinacy is an owl:Class (a gUFO AbstractIndividualType / QualityValue type), and its instances (crisp, vague, fuzzy, probabilistic, disputed) are first-class, referenceable, and co-equal value individuals. There is no 'preferred' determinacy (Principle 9). ONTOLOGICAL STATUS: gmeow:hasDeterminacy is an ObjectProperty (not an AnnotationProperty), because determinacy is a facet of the VALUE, not metadata ABOUT the claim. It is orthogonal to gmeow:confidence (epistemic) and to gmeow:standpointModality (belief force). SCOPE: Applies universally \u2014 a gender may be fuzzy, a date vague, a boundary probabilistic, a SLAM cell probabilistic, a contested fact disputed."

# # REFUSED (Principle 5 — no faithful external term): gmeow:determinacyCrisp has no clean Wikidata / ontology alignment. 'Crisp set' is the mathematical opposite of fuzzy set, but no stable QID names the concept directly; 'exactness' (Q89694598) and 'accuracy and precision' (Q272035) are about measurement error, not set-membership boundary. GMEOW retains the term without alignment rather than force a weak match.

# # REFUSED (Principle 5): gmeow:hasDeterminacy has no faithful external property alignment. Schema.org, GeoSPARQL, PROV-O, CIDOC-CRM, and DOLCE+DnS carry no direct 'determinacy of a value' property; the concept is novel.
# # REFUSED (Principle 5): gmeow:determinacyModel has no faithful external property alignment. It is the frame-level default for a ReferenceFrame, a GMEOW-specific construct.

column7: gmeow:Determinacy is declared rdfs:subClassOf gufo:QualityValue in the ontology; the alignment makes the dependency explicit in the mapping layer
BFO 'quality' is a high-level ontological category, not a value individual type; only a loose relatedMatch is warranted
Wikidata 'disputed' sourcing qualifier; the closest structured external term for a contested/undecided value
